hints: At the maximum x=a, differentiate y=√x sin2x with the product and chain rules and set the derivative to zero.
Multiply the stationary equation by 2√a to remove the denominator.
Rearrange sin2a+4a cos2a=0 and divide by cos2a to obtain the required tangent relation.
walkthrough:
Differentiate $y = x^{1/2}\sin(2x)$ using the product rule $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(uv) = u'v + uv'$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x^{1/2}) = \dfrac{1}{2}x^{-1/2} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}$$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(\sin(2x)) = 2\cos(2x)$$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\sin(2x) + 2\sqrt{x}\cos(2x)$$

Set the derivative equal to zero at the stationary point $M$ where $x = a$:
$$\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{a}}\sin(2a) + 2\sqrt{a}\cos(2a) = 0$$

ai_rubric.Finding Stationary Points: Applies the product rule to differentiate; Concludes with $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\sin2x+2\sqrt{x}\cos2x$; At $x=a$, $\sin2a+4a\cos2a=0$, hence $\tan2a=-4a$.

hints: Define the radian-mode root function f(x)=tan2x+4x from part (a).
Evaluate f(0.9) and f(0.95) with enough digits to show their opposite signs.
Use continuity on this interval to conclude that the root a lies strictly between the endpoints.
walkthrough:
Define the continuous function $g(x) = \tan(2x) + 4x$ based on the equation from part (a):
$$g(x) = \tan(2x) + 4x$$

State the conclusion from the change of sign:
$$\text{Since } g(0.9) < 0 \text{ and } g(0.95) > 0, \text{ and } g(x) \text{ is continuous on } [0.9, 0.95],$$
$$\text{there is a root } a \text{ such that } 0.9 < a < 0.95.$$

ai_rubric.Numerical Root Bracketing: Endpoint evaluations at 0.9 and 0.95 establish the sign change or ordering. Endpoint evaluation gives $f(x)=\tan2x+4x$, $f(0.9)=-0.686\ldots<0$ and $f(0.95)=0.873\ldots>0$, so $0.9<a<0.95$.

hints: If the sequence converges to a, replace both xₙ and xₙ₊₁ by a in the iterative formula.
Rearrange the fixed-point equation to π−2a=tan⁻¹(4a).
Take tangent in radians and use tan(π−2a)=−tan2a to recover tan2a=−4a, identifying the limit with the root from part (a).
walkthrough:
Assume the sequence converges to a limit $\alpha$. Then $\alpha$ must satisfy the fixed-point equation:
$$\alpha = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\pi - \tan^{-1}(4\alpha)\right)$$

Multiply both sides by 2 and isolate $\tan^{-1}(4\alpha)$:
$$2\alpha = \pi - \tan^{-1}(4\alpha)$$
$$\tan^{-1}(4\alpha) = \pi - 2\alpha$$

Take the tangent of both sides, using $\tan(\pi - \theta) = -\tan\theta$:
$$4\alpha = \tan(\pi - 2\alpha) = -\tan(2\alpha)$$
$$\tan(2\alpha) = -4\alpha$$

Since $a$ is the unique root of $\tan(2x) = -4x$ in $(0.9, 0.95)$, the limit $\alpha$ equals $a$:
$$\text{Hence, if the sequence converges, it converges to } a.$$

ai_rubric.Fixed-Point Iteration: Gives $a=\frac12(\pi-\tan^{-1}(4a))$ and rearrange to $\pi-2a=\tan^{-1}(4a)$. Gives $\tan(\pi-2a)=4a$ and rearrange to $\tan2a=-4a$. At convergence, $a=\frac12(\pi-\tan^{-1}(4a))$, so $\pi-2a=\tan^{-1}(4a)$ and hence $\tan2a=-4a$.

hints: Start with x₀=0.900000 and feed each output back into the formula, recording every iterate to 6 decimal places.
Continue until the iterates justify rounding the limit to 4 decimal places.
walkthrough:
Substitute the starting value $x_1 = 0.9$ into $x_{n+1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\pi - \tan^{-1}(4x_n)\right)$ using radian mode:
$$x_2 = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\pi - \tan^{-1}(4 \times 0.9)\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}(\pi - \tan^{-1}(3.6)) = \dfrac{1}{2}(3.141593 - 1.299847) \approx 0.920872$$

Compute successive iterates to 6 decimal places:
$$x_3 = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\pi - \tan^{-1}(4 \times 0.920872)\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}(\pi - \tan^{-1}(3.683488)) \approx 0.917944$$
$$x_4 = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\pi - \tan^{-1}(4 \times 0.917944)\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}(\pi - \tan^{-1}(3.671776)) \approx 0.918347$$
$$x_5 = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\pi - \tan^{-1}(4 \times 0.918347)\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}(\pi - \tan^{-1}(3.673388)) \approx 0.918292$$
$$x_6 = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\pi - \tan^{-1}(4 \times 0.918292)\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}(\pi - \tan^{-1}(3.673168)) \approx 0.918299$$

Conclude with the value of $a$ rounded to 4 decimal places:
$$\text{Both } 0.918292 \text{ and } 0.918299 \text{ round to } 0.9183:$$
$$a = 0.9183$$

ai_rubric.Fixed-Point Iteration: Substitution into $a$ gives consecutive iterates $0.9183\to0.91825\to0.91835$, converging to $a=0.9183$; for example, starting with $x_0=0.900000$: $x_1=0.920872$, $x_2=0.917944$, $x_3=0.918347$, $x_4=0.918292$, $\ldots$.
